title: Could a Modern Engine on a Pentium Have Beaten Kasparov?
summary: A new article examines whether a modern chess engine running on 1990s Pentium-class hardware could have defeated Garry Kasparov in 1996. It uses the counterfactual to explore how much of modern chess-engine strength comes from algorithmic improvements in evaluation and search versus gains from raw hardware performance.
